entries.title: 3 Ping Pong Sounds 8 bit style
entries.author: captaincrunch80
entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> (This package is bundled with the graphics http://opengameart.org/content/full-8bit-ping-pong-set ) The good old Ping Pong game is still the best to warm up for a game programming career. Don't believe it? I tell you why: You will need to get a lag free rendering or drawing solution for all situations, that will teach you a lot, even on this low level and is essential. You need to take care of game mechanics to make the game fun to play The player stick should not be at the target location instantly, that is boring and not old school (You remember the atari potentiometers?). Colision Detection (what about the small sides of the stick?). Nice reflecting of the ball (that one has to be perfect and involves a tiny glimse of unavoidable maths for game programmers) Constraints - The sticks must stop at the walls. Last but not least the sounds have to be syncronized with the screen action. Lag free. You can do what freshly baken game designers should and change the mechanics to make it more interesting. Like some friction on the sticks. An AI for the enemy stick, so you can play alone and have a good but satisfying challenge? Or something real crazy... Feel free, be creative! Have fun! Yours, captaincrunch80

These sounds are very quiet and you will have to normalize them using for example Audacity < http://www.audacity.sf.net/> or Sox < http://sox.sf.net> (for Sox see "Sox script for normalizing and converting mp3 & wav files to an Asterisk friendly format" < http://www.voip-info.org/wiki/view/sox> ) Also note that the sounds have a sample rate of 96000, this might cause problems with some soundcards and should be cut down to 44100 I guess. Do what you want with them or see the license as "Public Domain Dedication" or "CC0".

"Beats Warrior: Nian" is the first game I made, and I have already landed on Steam. I used the generator to make a bunch of 8bit sound effects in the production process, and now share these sound effects for free for developers. I don't change the file name very much, and most of them can be experienced through my game. The sound effect can be unrestrictedly quoted, reprinted, re-adapted, re-published, and used for commercial purposes, and the user may not mark the source and author of the creation. But if you like and are willing to mark the source and author of the creation, the welcome label is: "Beats Warrior: Nian" Developer - Liujiajun If you have any developers who want to communicate, please feel free to contact. My contact email: liujiajun@qq.com August 5, 2019

entries.title: Battle at sea
entries.author: Thimras
entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> Sounds of naval battle between sailing ships. Cannons firing, misses splashing into the sea, hits bursting decks and exploding powder reserves. Attacking a fortified structure has hits crumbling stone/mortar and possibly drop into the sea. A collision between the ships with flapping sails has wood creaking and breaking, with one version having sailors cry out in anticipation. The destruction of ships comes in versions of two different lengths, both with several explosions and the sea claiming the burning remains of the vessel. This sound set was created as part of the OpenGameArt Winter Jam 2022 for the amazing game "War Ships" by Raghunandan M. A. - check it out here: https://raghunandan.itch.io/war-ships .

entries.title: Dialog vocal samples
entries.author: MirceaKitsune
entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> Many RPG games use short vocal samples to further the personalities of their characters (Undertale is a great example). A sounds is played as each letter is printed in the dialog box, to better simulate that character speaking out. As there's a major lack of such audios especially under a free license, I decided to create my own. I used Espeak and Audacity to generate them, and came up with 32 vocal samples in total. This consists of 4 tone sets representing: Standard male, deep male, standard female, light female, demon voice, quick voice, whisper sound, robot beeping. Designed for the OHRRPGCE RPG engine: http://rpg.hamsterrepublic.com/ohrrpgce

entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> First Light Particles is a calm, atmospheric piano piece designed for story-driven games, exploration scenes, dream sequences, and emotional cutscenes. entries.title: Insect or alien scream
entries.author: qubodup
entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> I created this, after getting inspired by this gun sounds tutorial . What I did was (In Audacity terms): 1. Record letting air out of a balloon 2. Fade in 3. Reverse 4. Change speed (50%) 5. Slide Time Scale/Pitch Shift (Initial tempo: 0%, Final tempo: 92%, initial shift: 0, final shift: 0, no DTS) about 5 times 6. Change tempo (50%) 7. Normalize (-0.5) In Daft Punk terms that would have been: Fade it, flip it, slow it, shift it, slow it, normalize and save it.

entries.title: Interactive JRPG music in FMOD Studio
entries.author: SubspaceAudio
entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> This is an interactive exploration + battle music combo. The music fits JRPGs and other RPG and fantasy settings with active combat system. My video demonstration of this music and engine in action: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7WWUfdo9gHE The audio middleware engine used for this is FMOD Studio which is easy to integrate into engines like Unity or Unreal Engine. The seamless switching between these music segments is done via state parameter that is either 0 (for exploration) or 1 (for battle). FMOD is free to use if your game development budget is under $500 000. Download latest FMOD API: https://www.fmod.com/download This music is part of the 400 Indie Game Music Loops pack available from: https://subspaceaudio.itch.io/indie-game-music-loops If you also need sound effects for your game, there's the gigantic 1000 Retro Sound Effects pack available from itch.io: https://subspaceaudio.itch.io/1000-retro-sound-effects Want to get SERIOUS about sound effects? There's also the astronomical 6000 Retro Sound Effects collection available from itch.io to cover all your retro sound needs for life: https://subspaceaudio.itch.io/6000-retro-sound-effects

entries.title: Old Tricks
entries.author: Zane Little Music
entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> UPDATE: Another Bag of Chips is now available for free on Bandcamp and Ko-Fi for free! Download the album from there to get all the bonus content including looping versions of every track! ------------------ Here's the next freebie from my next album! This old dog's old tricks ain't broke, so he don't fix 'em. And then he SAVES THE WORLD!!!!!!!!!!!!! It's becoming clear to me that after this album is complete, I am ready to move on to some new stuff. I still have some other albums in the works that I have to finish though, so I'm not totally off the hook yet! Also I won't be quitting music, I just want to work on music projects that I can spend more time on and express myself with. I'm a lad with a SOUL and FEELINGS and I gotta get those out there somehow. Anywho, there's only 3 tracks left for this project! It's looking like March or April will probably be the time of completion!! Thank you to everyone who's stuck around and enjoyed the project so far. It will be on Bandcamp for free when it's all done! Of course, if you are able to spare a buck or two for the album when it's out, it surely goes a long way! Either way, I appreciate you. Enjoy!

entries.title: Park ambiences
entries.author: Thimras
entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> 3 recordings of ambience in different parts of a public park. One is close to a copse of trees, featuring birds chattering before the rain. The second is a recording of a small river with water falling over a low step, with some bird calls and frogs and other wildlife. The third is recorded in an open field with more intense wind. All recordings were made in a public park in Adelaide, South Australia, in winter. All files are recorded at 48kHz. To keep the filesize under 100mb, the two largest recordings have a bit depth of 16 bit. The park_ambience_wind file has a bit depth of 24 bit.

entries.title: Peacock scream
entries.author: qubodup
entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> I got permission to extract the peacock's voice from this youtube video ! The discussion: From: Iwan 'qubodup' To: popthebubbles4 Subject: Feathery proposal for video games Message: Hello, the following might sound weirder than a peacock scream, I'm looking for animal voices on Youtube, to extract their sound and make them available for use in video game development on http://opengameart.org and found the reply to your proposal to the peacock to be of high quality and probably very useful. Would you or your ..friend mind if I extracted his first scream from the video and made them available on said site, giving it to the public domain? Everybody would be free to do whatever they want with the files. My intension is to ease game developers' and other artists' work with that. I would give you and your feathery friend credit by linking to the video, unless you prefer that I do not (just say so). I will do nothing unless I get a green light from you. If you don't like what I ask for, ignore this message and I won't touch your videos in any way ;) Best regards Iwan ------------------------------------------------------ From: popthebubbles4 To: Iwan 'qubodup' Subject: Re: Feathery proposal for video games Message: Sure.

entries.title: Platformer Sounds: Terminal, Interaction, Door, Shots, Bang and Footsteps
entries.author: yd
entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> The sounds were made in a rather eclectic way. Something came from Freesound (CC0 stuff) and then went through the Audacity. Something has been taken from here and again went through Audacity filters. beep_message.ogg - a computer terminal console printing text, sci-fi tech style. Sounds like an irregular alarm clock or intruder alarm altert sound effect. boxopen.ogg - spacey and cool bang hit sound. cogs.ogg - speed up of rather synthesizer style mechanical motor cogs. door_open.ogg - loud sliding door barrier opening or closing. explode.ogg - simple destruction explosion. kill_shoot.ogg - firing a mashine gun round, has a fantasy or robot scream touch to it. landing.ogg - very blunt landing of a metal spaceship on the ground or of a cyborg on the floor. steps_chain.ogg - foot steps on various surfaces (including the remaining sounds) steps_platform2.ogg steps_platform.ogg steps_stairs1.ogg steps_stairs.ogg

На хуй! Охуеть! Пизда! Сука! Бля! Хуйня! Пиздец! Ебать! Заебись! Жопа! Ебаный! Пиздёж! F*ck! (They're common single word swears that mostly express "f*ck, sh*t, d*mn" about an unfavorable situation. Only a handful could also serve double-use as insults, like the classic Cyka and Blyat, but the rest not so much.) These are useful for game over screen sound bites, comedic character death sounds, ragdoll "pain" sounds, or for "access denied" moments in adventure games. ## Other Stuff Check out my other cool stuff: https://reactorcore.itch.io/ https://linktr.ee/reactorcore ## Contact mailto:reactorcoregames@gmail.com

entries.author: Yoiyami
entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> Starfield Romance is a soft, emotional space-themed soundtrack built around gentle piano, airy pads, floating harmonies, and subtle cosmic shimmer. It expresses the feeling of: •drifting through a quiet starfield •looking up at the night sky with someone important •cosmic stillness mixed with human warmth •soft wonder, nostalgia, and distant memories Musically, the track features: •transparent piano motifs •slow harmonic shifts with blue-tinted modal color •delicate high-frequency shimmer like stardust •subtle low-end pulses suggesting cosmic motion •no percussion, no groove — only floating movement Perfect for: •space exploration games •visual novels (romantic, emotional, night scenes) •stargazing cutscenes •dream sequences •sci-fi menus / title screens •atmospheric RPG zones •quiet moments of reflection or confession This track is CC0 (public domain). Free for use in any project — commercial or hobby — without attribution.

entries.title: The Budding of Consciousness – CC0 Ambient / Minimalist Theme Yoiyami Blue Series – No.4
entries.author: Yoiyami
entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> The Budding of Consciousness is a gentle, minimal ambient piece expressing the moment when awareness first begins to form — soft, fragile, and full of quiet wonder. The music features: •warm, evolving piano colors •delicate harmonic movements with blue-toned modal tension •subtle shimmering pads like light filtering through water •slow emotional growth, rising and falling like breath •faint low-frequency pulses suggesting heartbeat or awakening •no percussion, no groove — pure atmospheric flow The mood is: •introspective •serene •slightly mystical •peaceful, but with a sense of quiet expansion Perfect for: •prologue scenes •character introspection •dream sequences •meditation or memory fragments •slow exploration •“first awakening” moments in sci-fi or fantasy games •philosophical / emotional storytelling •menu or pause screens with calm ambience This track is CC0 (public domain) — completely free for any use.

entries.title: The Free Firearm Sound Library
entries.author: bart
entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> From The Free Firearm Sound Library homepage : The firearm sound library was the brainchild of a team of college students with a mutual passion for the audio and visual arts. In November, 2013 we launched a Kickstarter campaign to develop an extensive open source firearm sound effects library, and on December 7, 2013 our project was funded by an incredible group of backers and we went into full tilt production. This website serves to connect our backers with our two libraries, as well as to give credit to the backers who made it all possible. Along with the availability of these sounds comes the need to understand their proper application. The metadata included in the sound files along with some instructional videos will help make these sounds serve you to their full potential. Our team holds CC0 NO RIGHTS RESERVED for this library. It may be used without royalty or credit (though we would love to hear how you've used our sounds) for any application, personal or professional. Have at it! Please note that OGA is not affiliated with this project, and as such, we encourage you to visit their site so as to make sure you're getting the latest version of the files: http://freefirearmsfx.com raw prepared Also note that their website includes instructions along with the raw versions of the sound effects, which are not archived here. Big thanks to their team and all of their Kickstarter supporters for this amazing colle

entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> 3-chord jam with a high-energy vibe. Same chords as ( https://opengameart.org/content/osiris-monolith ) although different key. Pretty repetitious, so key changes periodically to break the monotony. You may or may not like that; at some point, I'd like to add real parts B, C, etc and cut back some of the key changes. A little backdrop: this isn't a sandy scene, but a sunset upon a desert painted black & white by an advanced civilization, and carved with their heavy machinery. Upon completion, every inch of the great pyramid of Giza was a reflective white limestone, sitting atop flat pavement made of carved black basalt stones, as far as the eye can see. This tune accompanies the creation of those pyramids, as I see it, as more evidence is beginning to show! Piano version available and MID for melodies.

entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> A serene Yoiyami-core theme built around deep-blue emotional colors. Soft piano leads the piece with stepwise melodies and subtle fourth leaps, supported by warm, organic bass tones. Airy pads drift like quiet night air, while shimmering electric guitar echoes and a gentle shakuhachi-like breath instrument add a hint of Japanese ambience. No heavy groove — only fluid motion, modal tension (4-5-6), and calm introspective flow. Perfect for: •RPG / adventure exploration •fantasy worlds •visual novels •emotional cutscenes •menus & title screens •peaceful ambience Format: High-quality stereo mix License: CC0 (free for all uses, commercial or non-commercial)

entries.title: Zippo click sound
entries.author: qubodup
entries.description: field-name-body field-type-text-with-summary field-label-hidden"> I was fooling around with a mic (a shure SM 58) and recorded myself opening and closing a zippo lighter. Well, one of the clicky sounds that I recorded sounded nice enough to me for a sound of opening the main menu while in game or the like. Anyway, do whatever you wish with it, here it is in flac format. http://forums.parpg.net/index.php/topic,956.0.html
